Hi Rishi,

Apologies for the urgency — over the last 6 hours we’ve seen ~150 failed card charges across multiple customers. Declines look like issuer-level BIN blocking: same BINs get ~20-30% failure rates while others are fine. Acquirers flagged the pattern and Stripe put a temporary hold on automated retries.

We’re past the immediate retry window and worried about customer churn. Can Redwood pause auto-collection attempts for these invoices and give us guidance on the safest retry cadence? Also need guidance on messaging to end-customers and whether Redwood can surface a card-update workflow inline (we currently have a basic hosted update page).

I attached decline_samples_oct02.csv with representative transactions and logged a Stripe ticket (789123) — attaching the support PDF they returned.

Looking for a plan by EOD so we can triage with our CFO.

Thanks,

Thanks for the sample data and the heads-up, Alyssa — sorry you’re in the middle of this. We’ll treat it as a high-priority collection incident. Proposing immediate containment + recovery steps below:

1) Pause Redwood auto-retries for the affected invoice cohort (we can target by BIN range or by the transaction list you sent). I’ll schedule the pause now; confirm if you want us to backfill retries later.
2) Enable card-update modal on the invoice success page and send a short email to impacted customers with a direct card-update link (we can host the flow; it supports tokenization and SCA).
3) Staggered retry policy: escalate to manual pre-authorizations with 3DS where supported — start with low-frequency retries (24h, 72h) and limit attempts per-customer to 2 to avoid additional issuer friction.
4) Evidence & chargeback prevention: ask customers to whitelist our charge descriptor and offer a friendly in-app notice explaining the attempt was declined by issuer. Marcus, can your team prepare the 3DS proof and AVS/transaction logs Stripe will need?
5) Liaise with Stripe: request BIN-unblock or clearer decline reason. Alyssa, please confirm whether Stripe supplied an acquirer-level remediation ETA in ticket 789123.

I’ve paused retries for the sample cohort and attached a short playbook we use for BIN-bloc incidents. If you want we can open a joint bridge with Stripe support and Zeno payments to drive the unblock.

Next actions: Alyssa to confirm unblock ETA and whether Zeno wants Redwood to host the card-update modal. Marcus to assemble evidence artifacts. Laura to approve any credit/waiver proposals if we recommend issuing credits.

—Rishi

Hi all,

I pulled the logs and cross-checked tokenization and AVS fields for the CSV rows — a few notes:
- For ~60% of the failed rows the transactions completed 3DS lookup but the issuer returned a hard decline (code 05/issuer_reject).
- A subset show AVS mismatch (zip vs billing) — likely cardholder entry error or gateway formatting differences.
- No evidence of lost tokens or gateway-side timeouts.

What I’ll do now:
- Package 3DS challenge evidence and the associated assertion IDs (will upload to the Stripe ticket).
- Produce a short CSV for Stripe with BIN ranges and sample token IDs (redacted PAN) to speed their acquirer query.
- Stand by for a joint bridge if Stripe requests a live session.

Alyssa — to minimize churn I recommend: (a) immediate one-time email asking customers to update payment method with a direct link to the hosted update page; (b) offer a one-time courtesy 7-day extension on impacted invoices while we escalate. Laura — can you confirm a 7-day extension credit policy for impacted customers?

Marcus

Hi team,

We’ve investigated ticket 789123. Findings: the issuing bank has enacted a BIN-level rule due to suspected fraud across a handful of merchants. This is an issuer-side action and cannot be removed by the acquirer or Stripe immediately. Recommended steps:

- Gather detailed evidence (3DS authentication traces, AVS/CCV matching results) and submit to the issuing bank via acquirer request.
- Encourage affected cardholders to contact their issuing bank to lift the block; this is often the quickest resolution for commercial BIN blocks.
- Implement a staggered retry policy and remove aggressive automated retries to avoid increased decline rates and potential issuer-level escalations.

We can expedite an acquirer inquiry if you provide the BIN ranges and sample tokenized transaction IDs — please upload via the secure ticket link.

Regards,
Stripe Risk Team
